title: MouseWithoutBorders "Share Clipboard" option + Intel I219-V ethernet adapter crashes Windows network stack

judgment.rationale: The report describes a serious delayed network failure with a specific Intel I219-V adapter and Share Clipboard enabled, and says the reporter avoids the feature. There is no crash dump, event evidence, or controlled current-version test isolating clipboard sharing from other MWB activity.
evidence: Reported adapter is Intel I219-V (hardware ID PCI\VEN_8086&DEV_15BC...).
Issue appears after several hours with Share Clipboard enabled and is reported across Windows versions.
Windows reports Ethernet connected while communication stops; no comments or attachments are present.
judgment.recommended_action: Request adapter driver and time-correlated system events, plus a controlled test disabling only Share Clipboard.

fix_assessment.rationale: A temporal association is reported, but there is no evidence whether clipboard IPC, NIC driver, or another network component causes failure. No PowerToys code fix is grounded yet.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders clipboard sharing is associated with delayed loss of network communication on an Intel I219-V system.
known_information: Author workaround is using Windows clipboard sync.
Failure is described as total connectivity loss while Ethernet remains connected.
No NIC driver version or event/error codes are stated.
inferences: Adapter or filter-driver stack may be involved, but causality beyond enabling Share Clipboard is not established.
issue_context.analysis: Use a controlled setting comparison and OS network events to localize the failure; do not ask for unrelated PowerToys logs.
initial_investigation: Read full issue report; no comments or attached files are present.
Pinned MWB source includes clipboard helper and network/socket paths, but report lacks timestamped evidence linking those paths to adapter failure.

information_gaps.information: The network adapter driver version and any Windows System events at the time connectivity stops; also whether disabling only Share Clipboard prevents recurrence while Mouse Without Borders remains enabled.
information_gaps.why_needed: Report identifies Intel I219-V and delayed network failure with Share Clipboard enabled, but lacks time-correlated evidence, driver version, or a controlled test isolating clipboard sharing.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: If issue recurs, note time and export relevant Windows System events for the Intel adapter/network stack; report driver version and whether disabling Share Clipboard alone prevents recurrence. Do not include packet captures or credentials.

comment.body: Thanks for including the adapter model and workaround. Could you share the Intel adapter driver version and any Windows System events recorded when connectivity stops? If safe to retry, please compare with Mouse Without Borders still enabled but Share Clipboard alone disabled, and say whether the failure returns. This will help separate the clipboard feature from the NIC/driver path without requesting packet captures or credentials.
